transcript: So I've actually been in contact with Chairman Mike Boss, who's a great guy. He's the chairman of the Vietnam Affairs community. Now in the 80s, it was a little over 70%. For those of us who are in the military, it's the same equivalent when we'd get equipment that would be procured from someone who doesn't actually go into the field and we'd look at it and be, what the hell is this? And how am I supposed to use it? And it's the same way in Congress. So we are looking at VA overhaul. We are looking at the ideas of ensuring that we get the necessary tools and kits. And one of the things that I talked about was that We don't need to continue to spend, as an example, $100 billion on a new VA hospital in a metropolitan area that has nine other capable hospitals. We just need access in the same level of cares. We need to be utilizing that $100 billion to actually go into the urban areas. And so getting the necessary ability to try and get hospitals over VA into rural areas where you don't have to drive an hour and a half and two hours. The idea of being able to utilize the existing echelons of care that are available to us in our own cities and districts, I think this is a great first step in opening up a platform that allows us to have more visibility and to address more of the issues, but also to allocate necessary funding into TBI, PTSD, and other types of mental health issues for treatments. One of the things I've seen recently, which is incredible and very, in my opinion, encouraging is the hyperbarometric pressure chambers, where we've actually seen a 100% turnaround for those with TBI and PTSD who's actually gone through one treatment. So the idea that we can continue to invest in these things, the idea that we can continue to have people in Congress who understand military veteran needs and transitional needs and mental health capabilities, because I just spoke with at VEI. VEI thinks they're serving a purpose of entrepreneurship, but in reality, what they're doing is they're actually giving military soldiers' mission and purpose, and that's all we ever want. Military events are very simplistic. We're very old-fashioned. We want to have mission and purpose, and we want to be able to do protection and provision of our family. And if we can't do those things, we don't have purpose. We don't feel there's a reason and a use for us here. And so the VA is addressing these issues, not just for suicide prevention and awareness, but TBI-PTS utilization, tri-care extension, VA overhaul for utilization of our existing echelons of care, and hopefully getting the wait times down to where we can get treated the same way that we got treated when we were in the military. We're willing to wear that uniform and die for this nation. Our nation should be willing to do what they have to do and die for us.
